messages.subject: Re: result of mdply: leave out the parameters
parts:
Oops, I hadn't realized that for some reason I wasn't running the
latest version of plyr, despite my complete reinstalling of R two days
ago.

maply() does work as I wanted with plyr 1.1.

Thanks,

baptiste


On Sun, Aug 1, 2010 at 2:57 PM, Eduardo Leoni <e.l...@gmail.com> wrote:
> Perhaps you should update your version of plyr?
>
>> is.matrix(maply(params, foo))
> [1] TRUE
>
> other attached packages:
> [1] plyr_1.1
>
>
> On Sun, Aug 1, 2010 at 9:44 AM, baptiste auguie <bapt...@googlemail.com> wrote:
>> Are you sure?
>>
>>
>> library(plyr)
>> params <- expand.grid(a=1:2, b=1:2)
>> foo <- function(a,b) c(rnorm(1), rnorm(1))
>> str(maply(params, foo))
>>
>> gives me a cubic array.
>>
>> Thanks,
>>
>> baptiste
>>
>>
>>
>> On Sun, Aug 1, 2010 at 2:32 PM, Eduardo Leoni <e.l...@gmail.com> wrote:
>>> Do you need a data frame? If the output of foo is a vector maply will
>>> do what you want.
>>>
>>> On Sun, Aug 1, 2010 at 6:09 AM, baptiste auguie <bapt...@googlemail.com> wrote:
>>>> I did try maply too, but for some reason the results are coerced into
>>>> a higher-dimensional object or in a different structure (array of
>>>> lists).
>>>>
>>>> library(plyr)
>>>> params <- expand.grid(a=1:2, b=1:2)
>>>> foo <- function(a,b) data.frame(x=rnorm(1), y=rnorm(1))
>>>> maply(params, foo)
>>>> ##    b
>>>> ## a   1      2
>>>> ##   1 List,2 List,2
>>>> ##   2 List,2 List,2
>>>>
>>>> The closest I can get to the result I want (an efficient one-liner,
>>>> basically) is with mlply,
>>>>
>>>> results <- do.call(rbind, mlply(params, foo))
>>>>
>>>> Thanks,
>>>>
>>>> baptiste
